title: telemetry-friendly-schema-errors-with-streaming-checkpoints-and-toolcall-hints
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Customers need deterministic errors from structured-output endpoints that are actionable for client SDKs and observability stacks while preserving streaming latency and tool/function-calling semantics. This PR introduces a telemetry-friendly error contract for response_format=json_schema used with streaming and tool calls, plus a lightweight streaming checkpoint used to fence tool invocations for safe resumption. Summary: 1) Introduce a thin header X-Redwood-Contract-Error that surfaces a short machine code (e.g., SCHEMA_MISMATCH, STREAM_TRUNCATED, TOOL_FENCE_VIOLATION) and a stable telemetry tag. 2) Add an in-stream checkpoint token ("checkpoint_id") emitted before tool/function calls and at schema validation boundaries so clients can resume from the last acknowledged checkpoint on retry. 3) Extend OpenAI-compat mapping so legacy clients receive compatible error types but SDKs can opt-in to structured error payloads via Accept: application/vnd.redwood+json. 4) Implement a runtime validator that performs streaming-aware schema checks: lightweight progressive validation with final strict pass before commit. Design details: - Checkpointing: the runtime emits a minimal JSON fragment "{\"_checkpoint\": \"<uuid>\"}" as a discrete event on the stream prior to any tool call or schema-critical token boundary. Checkpoints are advisory by default; in strict mode they become fencing points (the runtime records tool-call side effects only after the strict checkpoint is acknowledged by the client via a follow-up acknowledgment API or by an idempotent toolcall token). - Error contract: errors include three fields in the header and, when Accept indicates Redwood structured error support, the final error event includes a machine_code, human_message, client_hint (e.g., "retry_with_backoff"/"adjust_schema"), and telemetry_tags. When mapping to OpenAI-compat errors the runtime preserves the human_message and maps machine_code to a short code placed in error.type for easy ingestion by third-party clients. - Streaming validation: to avoid latency regressions we run a progressive validator that checks incremental token sequences for major structural violations (unclosed arrays/objects, type mismatches that are deterministically provable) and defers non-deterministic checks until finalization. On finalization we perform full jsonschema validation; if strict mode is enabled we emit SCHEMA_STRICT_VIOLATION and close the stream with a clear checkpoint id for restart. - Tool/function-calling safety: toolcalls now include a toolcall_token and a pre-call checkpoint emitted in-stream. If a tool reports a side-effect failure, the runtime includes TOOL_FENCE_VIOLATION with the checkpoint id so downstream systems can reconcile or retry idempotently. Backward compatibility: older clients get minimal header-only errors (no structured JSON) and will see canonical OpenAI-style error.text. New SDKs (python/ts/go) will decode structured errors and surface client_hint and telemetry_tags in exceptions/LogRecords. Migration: - Console and Optimize teams will receive a small telemetry column for contract error codes. - SDK teams get a small API addition: Response.contract_error (nullable) and Stream.on_checkpoint(callback). Testing: unit tests for progressive validator, e2e integration tests with the tool-runner (simulated idempotent and non-idempotent tool outcomes), load tests to verify <2% p50 latency impact under typical streaming workloads. Checklist: - [x] Runtime: emit checkpoint tokens and structured header - [x] Runtime: progressive validator + final strict pass - [x] API: Accept header negotiation and OpenAI-mapping layer - [x] SDK: python/ts basic decoding and streaming callbacks - [x] Docs: Console and API docs describing new headers and migration - [x] Telemetry: contract error tags in trace/span attributes - [x] Load tests run on perf-canary Observability notes: added contract_error and checkpoint_id as stable span attributes (redwood.contract_error, redwood.checkpoint_id) and a dashboard tile that breaks down top 10 contract_error codes. Security: no secrets exposed; checkpoint tokens are UUIDv4 and do not encode PII. Related: ENG-2145 for validator work, PM-87 for product acceptance criteria, SUP-4123 for a troubleshooting playbook. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable structured headers and checkpoints in canary region with feature flag rschema.streaming.telemetry=false (header-only) - Stage 2: enable progressive validation and sdk opt-in for structured errors - Stage 3: strict-mode gating for paid tiers only and documentation updates - Rollback: feature flags to disable checkpoint emission and revert to legacy OpenAI-compatible behavior.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice end-to-end. Two requests: 1) add a clear TL;DR for SDK consumers in the top of docs so they can opt in quickly, 2) ensure checkpoint UUIDs are rotated per request so they cannot be guessed across sessions.
Priya Nair (author): Added TL;DR to docs and ensured checkpoint UUID is per-request (see emitter.go change).
Marco Liu: Can we include a small backoff recommendation in the client_hint? Many infra teams want deterministic retry windows for billing reconciliation.
Priya Nair: Added client_hint examples (retry_with_backoff: 2s, exponential up to 30s) and added in docs.
release_notes: Added streaming checkpoints and structured contract error telemetry for response_format=json_schema. New header X-Redwood-Contract-Error with machine codes and opt-in structured error payloads. SDKs updated to surface checkpoints and structured errors. Backward compatible with OpenAI-compat clients.
notes: Canary observations: small uptick in error telemetry during first day as customers opt-in; no increased tail latency observed in perf-canary runs.
Follow-ups: 1) automated client-acknowledgment API for strict checkpoints (ENG-2210), 2) richer tooling for automated schema-guided prompt repair in Optimize (PM-121).
